es: Identificar el punto, la razón, el ejemplo y el cierre en respuestas improvisadas y reconocer cuál está mejor ordenada.

prompt.es: Responde a la pregunta sorpresa en un minuto, con las cuatro partes.

answer.text: That's a tricky one, so let me think for a second. My stance is that a generalist has more options than a specialist. The main reason is that jobs change faster than any single specialist can follow. A generalist can move between fields, learn new tools and adapt when a company changes direction. For example, my cousin trained as a nurse, then worked in a hospital office, and now manages a small clinic. If she had stayed only a specialist, she would not have had those chances. Of course, specialists are important, and I would not want a generalist to be my doctor. Sorry, I'm rambling a little; let me go back to my point. What matters is that you commit to one stance early, and then you support it with a reason and an example. So, in short, I would rather be a generalist with one strong skill, because that mix gives me both skill and choices. That is my answer, and I hope it is clear.
